findings.title: Retained directory handle does not protect the selected pathname against replacement
findings.detail: Native fixture: qualificationGuardDirectory(directory,true) succeeds. While guard is open, os.Rename moves the final dispatch directory. A replacement private directory is created at the original pathname. Old/new directory IDs differ (same volume; low 5278472 versus 5278476 in this run), yet original guard.Check returns nil. qualificationOpenSource(originalPath,...,true), write, Sync and file.Check all succeed; bytes exist only in the replacement namespace and no receipt exists under the original held directory. Check verifies the original handle IDs against themselves, not the current selected pathname. Metadata-only directory handles therefore do not provide the promised final-directory rename exclusion on this Windows environment.
findings.fix: Keep selected namespace and actual child opens bound to the same native directory identity throughout the operation. Use a native handle/access/open strategy that demonstrably excludes rename/replacement, or open children relative to a validated retained directory handle with an equivalent namespace guarantee. Fail closed on drift; a saved handle ID or a pathname check without continuous binding is insufficient. Add the deterministic final-directory replacement regression and retain separate source-file write/flush/read continuity checks.
findings.limits: Owned fresh fixture and unexported production helpers through Go overlay; no actual cross-user attacker or original/production path was exercised. Ancestor root rename was denied in initial cut; selected final directory replacement succeeded. Separate native file handles correctly refused competing writes/deletes/renames.
